blocks.text: Setting up your patient tracking sheet

Efficiency starts with a clean structure. Avoid mixing data types in the same column. If you track patient IDs, format them as text to keep leading zeros. Select your ID column, right click, and choose Format Cells > Text.
Using data validation for consistent entry

Consistency helps when you run reports. Use Data Validation to create drop down lists for statuses like Pending, Approved, or Denied. Go to Data > Data Validation > Allow > List. Enter your options separated by commas.

When your list grows, use filters to find specific patient records. Click any cell in your header row. Go to Data > Filter. Now you can click the small arrow in the header to show only specific insurance providers or referral types.
If your sheet feels slow, check if you have thousands of formulas referencing entire columns. Try to limit your formula ranges to the specific cells containing data.
blocks.title: Performance tip

blocks.text: Use conditional formatting to spot overdue authorizations. Select your date column. Go to Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Less Than. Enter =TODAY() to turn cells red if the date has passed.
